content: The accelerated national registration of WHO-prequalified in vitro diagnostics is detailed in Annex 4, with the document accessed on November 2, 2023. Additional references include Annex 17, accessed on October 9, 2023, and WHO's webpage on regulation and prequalification, which provides information on safety for medical devices, including in vitro diagnostics, accessed on January 14, 2024. Guidance documents for post-market surveillance and market surveillance of medical devices, including in vitro diagnostics, were accessed on October 9, 2023. Similarly, guidance for the procurement of in vitro diagnostics and related laboratory items and equipment was accessed on November 1, 2023. Annex 7 of TRS 1025 outlines good storage and distribution practices for medical products, with the document accessed on November 2, 2023. A best practices document and facilitator’s guide for developing a national laboratory strategic plan were accessed on November 2, 2023. Chapter 9 of the referenced material focuses on quality assurance for HIV testing services. ISO 15189:2022, which specifies requirements for quality and competence in medical laboratories, was accessed on November 2, 2023. The WHO guide for the Stepwise Laboratory Improvement Process Towards Accreditation (SLIPTA) in the African region was accessed on November 3, 2023. The Laboratory Quality Stepwise Implementation Tool was accessed on August 26, 2023. Operational characteristics of HIV assays, specifically rapid diagnostic tests for detecting HIV-1/2 antibodies, were detailed in Report 17, accessed on January 15, 2024. The consolidated guidelines on person-centered HIV strategic information, which emphasize strengthening routine data for impact, were accessed on October 3, 2023. A document on improving the quality of HIV-related point-of-care testing, ensuring the reliability and accuracy of test results, was accessed on November 3, 2023. The web annexes include systematic reviews and GRADE analyses addressing various HIV testing approaches. These include social network testing, HIV self-testing in health facilities, and the use of self-testing to support PrEP delivery. Modeling of HIV self-testing for oral PrEP scale-up in Kenya, including its impact on HIV drug resistance and outcomes, is also included. Additional annexes explore caregiver-assisted testing for children aged 18 months and older, the use of HIV recency testing in routine programmatic services, and the values and preferences of key populations in the Asia-Pacific region regarding HIV recency testing. Compiled case examples are also provided in the annexes.
